findings.finding: The 'billed yearly' half of the ticket has no acceptance criterion, and nothing in this repo can check it. All five criteria prove one thing: a lookup returns 990. Whether a customer is actually billed once a year depends entirely on the external callers. The plan's own risky_assumptions say so: priceFor's result is assumed to be 'the amount charged per billing period', and no interval is recorded anywhere. A caller only knows a key is yearly if it parses the key string. If any external caller charges priceFor(plan) on a fixed monthly cycle, a growth_annual customer is charged 990 every month: 11,880 a year instead of 990, a 12x overcharge. The same applies to any caller that shows the price as '/mo', computes MRR, or works out an upgrade difference such as priceFor(new) - priceFor(old) (growth to growth_annual would read as +891 for the same period). The human approved '990 a year' but was never asked whether the callers know growth_annual is yearly. That question appears only as an assumption, not in questions_for_human, so it was never answered.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a question for the founder and record the answer in human_decisions: 'External code that charges or displays priceFor(plan) has no interval information. Will it charge growth_annual once per year? Who owns making it do so?' If the answer is yes, add a criterion that the handover names this caller-side requirement explicitly: growth_annual returns a yearly amount and must be scheduled yearly. If the answer is no or unknown, the ticket cannot be finished by a PRICES entry alone. Either widen the scope with explicit founder approval, for example by exporting an interval for each key, which is a protected-file change beyond the one-entry approval, or stop and escalate.

findings.finding: The criterion 'The only change to src/billing.js is one new PRICES entry' is right, but it does not say how to check it. PRICES is a one-line object literal, so a builder who reformats it onto several lines 'for readability' breaks the criterion while every test still passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the check mechanical: `git diff src/billing.js` shows exactly one changed line, `{ starter: 49, growth: 99, scale: 199 }` becoming `{ starter: 49, growth: 99, scale: 199, growth_annual: 990 }`. No other line in the file changes.

findings.finding: The unknown-plan test could pass without proving the error message. A bare assert.throws(() => priceFor('growth_yearly')) passes on any throw. Near-miss keys a caller might realistically send are also not covered: 'Growth_Annual', 'growth-annual', 'growth_annual ' with a trailing space. These should throw, not be normalized into a match.
findings.suggested_fix: Use assert.throws(() => priceFor('growth_yearly'), { message: 'unknown plan: growth_yearly' }). Optionally add one near-miss case, such as 'Growth_Annual', to pin that no normalization happens.

findings.finding: The prototype-chain lookup is correctly kept out of scope, because the protected-file approval covers only this ticket's entry. But it is a live pricing defect: `plan in PRICES` lets priceFor('toString') and priceFor('constructor') return a function instead of throwing. Leaving it only in out_of_scope means it is never seen again. Also, any 'unknown plan' test the builder adds must not use a prototype key, or it will fail, or worse, be written to pin the buggy behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the handover file this as a separate ticket that needs its own founder sign-off. Keep negative-test inputs to non-prototype names.

findings.finding: FIXED: the 'billed yearly' major. Its core was that the caller-side interval question was never put to the human, so it was never answered. It now is: question 4, answered 'Go with your suggested answer'. On record: 990 is charged once a year, the external billing caller owns scheduling it yearly, and the caller-side work is a follow-up. The 12x-overcharge risk is now labelled ACCEPTED RISK in risky_assumptions, and the caller-side work is listed in out_of_scope. One part of the suggested fix was not taken, and this is the only remaining gap. The promise that 'handover files the caller-side work as a follow-up ticket' appears only in risky_assumptions and out_of_scope. Neither is an acceptance criterion. So nothing in review or verify checks that the follow-up ticket gets filed, and if it is dropped, the external callers never learn that growth_annual is yearly. The real-world exposure is partly self-limiting: PRICES is not exported, so a customer can only be put on growth_annual by a caller that already knows the key exists.
